reason: I get Korean food back home all the time for less, so on a Hawaii trip I'd rather spend my food budget on poke and plate lunches. Nineteen bucks for cold noodles plus tax and tip is around $23, and the kalbi at $39 is out of the question.
objection: It's a chain with branches in Japan, so it isn't a local Hawaii thing, and nothing here tells me it's worth paying Waikiki prices for noodles I can get at home.
would_change_my_mind: A lunch special around $14 to $15 with a side, or a friend telling me the noodles are clearly better than anything I can get on the mainland.
